niche_preference_profile: This user consistently prefers interfaces with strong visual hierarchy, clear section grouping, and card-based organization. They often favor centered modal/card presentations or clearly framed containers over edge-anchored sheets or flat continuous layouts. They like layouts that are scannable and structured, with explicit labels, grouped sections, and visible actions. Their density preference is context-dependent, but consistently resolves toward efficient information presentation: they prefer compact, organized, information-rich layouts when comparing data-heavy tools, while preferring simplified copy and reduced clutter when extra decoration or unnecessary content is present. Visually, they respond well to contrast, depth, dimmed backdrops, and framed surfaces, but generally reject noisy, cluttered, or weakly organized compositions. They also show repeated preference for rounded but controlled card treatments, concise direct controls, and stronger CTA emphasis when action is required.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers prominent titles, bold headlines, clearly separated sections, stronger grouping, and layouts where important content and actions are visually prioritized.
Prefers content organized into cards, list rows, grouped containers, or unified sections rather than flat pages, mixed flows, carousels, or loosely structured screens.

Prefers information to be efficiently organized and scannable: often favors compact, detail-rich lists or rows in utility contexts, but also prefers reduced copy and less unnecessary content when density comes from clutter rather than useful structure.
Prefers interfaces with obvious actions, strong CTA emphasis, visible button hierarchy, direct labels, and controls that feel explicit and easy to act on.
Prefers centered modal or overlay card presentations with isolated focus over bottom sheets, full-page document flows, or edge-anchored panels.
Prefers soft depth, subtle shadows, rounded cards, bordered containers, and visually framed surfaces, but generally not exaggerated pill shapes or overly inflated rounded panels.
Prefers cleaner compositions with fewer decorative elements, less visual noise, more disciplined spacing, and simpler iconography or imagery when extra elements do not improve comprehension.
